data.gender_notes: Champavati is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Champavati is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'Champaka' meaning 'jasmine flower'. In Hindu mythology, Champavati is the name of a beautiful and enchanting river nymph, who is known for her charm and allure. She is believed to possess the power to grant blessings of love, beauty, and prosperity. The name Champavati carries the meaning “Goddess of love and beauty” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Champavati usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of love and beauty and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Champavati belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of love and beauty.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Champavati total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

historical_references.reference: According to Hindu mythology, Champavati was a beautiful naga princess who lived in the River Godavari. She is said to have fallen in love with a human king, Rishyasringa, and bore him a son named Bhagiratha. However, her father, the serpent king Takshaka, became enraged at the defiance of his daughter and decided to flood the earth with the waters of the river to wipe out humanity. Bhagiratha then undertook a penance to bring the Gods of the Himalayas, including Lord Shiva, to the aid of humanity. Champavati's story is a tragic one, as she was eventually sacrificed by her father to quench his wrath.
